Subject: Tranche milestone schedule & annual prepay proposal for Skyline AI

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass proposal for a multi-year, annual-prepay structure that maps committed Dedicated capacity to milestone tranches (so you get predictable throughput as you ramp). High level:

- Term: 3 years, annual prepay (invoices at contract anniversary).
- Capacity commitments expressed as TPM-equivalent and GPU-equivalent tranches.
  - Year 1 (go-live): reserve 50 GPU-equivalent capacity (baseline tenant pool), 2.5M TPM monthly baseline.
  - Year 2 (scale): add 30 GPU-equivalent tranche at month 13, +1.5M TPM.
  - Year 3 (mature): add 20 GPU-equivalent tranche at month 25, +1.0M TPM.
- Pricing / term discounts: upfront annual prepay qualifies for stepped term discount (we've modeled a 7% effective discount Yr1, 12% Yr2, 18% Yr3 as an example) — exact percentages flexible based on final contract length and payment timing.
- Flex: ability to shift purchased TPM between availability zones within the same region; burst capacity policy and auto-fallback to compatible model variants.
- True-ups & credits: quarterly usage true-up with credit carryforward; unused capacity in a given year can be reallocated once per 12-month period (details in attached schedule).
- SLAs: latency targets and reserved throughput; priority queueing on Dedicated pool.

I've attached the SOW and a commit schedule workbook that shows invoices and suggested discount curves. If this direction looks reasonable I'll loop in Marissa (finance) and Ben (solutions) to finalize the invoice cadence, billing mechanics, and any procurement-friendly language (early termination, migration credits, audit logs).

Next steps suggested:
- Confirm whether Skyline prefers an annual invoice or quarterly invoicing with annual prepay (we can support either).
- Confirm the appetite for a steeper up-front discount (we can trade against acceleration of Year 2 capacity).
- If you want, we can convert this to a DocuSign-ready exhibit for procurement.

Thanks — look forward to your notes.

Best,
Chloe

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the workbook. A few clarifying Qs from procurement/finance before we loop legal:

1) Discount curve: can you show an alternative that front-loads the discount (e.g., 15% Yr1, 12% Yr2, 6% Yr3) vs the back-loaded structure you propose? CFO wants to see P&L impact year-by-year.
2) Early termination: what's your standard termination credit for prepay if we stop after Year 1? Any minimum notice?
3) True-up mechanics: you mentioned quarterly true-ups with credit carryforward — can unused prepaid capacity be converted to credits for other Redwood products (e.g., embeddings) or is it tied only to Dedicated throughput?
4) Invoice cadence: procurement prefers annual invoice but wants to see a sample invoice schedule that maps to our fiscal quarters (we close Q4 on Dec 31).
5) Migration / scale-up option: if we want to accelerate Year 2 capacity earlier than month 13, how flexible is reallocation and what are the price impacts?

Also, security will need the Dedicated deployment architecture doc; can you include the monitoring hooks and on-call SLA in the exhibit?

If you can get answers to the above and a DocuSign exhibit we can route to legal and procurement next week.

—Alex

Alex — thanks, good questions. Looping Ben and Marissa to respond and propose concrete options below.

Ben (solutions) — quick ask: can you confirm migration flexibility and monitoring hooks (include doc link).
Marissa (finance) — can you propose two discount curves (front-loaded and back-loaded) + sample invoice mapping to Skyline Qs.

Proposed answers (draft):
- Discount curves: we'll provide two model sheets. Our commercial play: higher up-front discount for earlier cash (we can offer 14% Yr1 / 10% Yr2 / 5% Yr3 for an aggressive front-load); alternatively the back-loaded you saw (7/12/18) preserves higher discounts as they scale. Either is possible; trade against final commitment length.
- Early termination: standard is pro rata refund of unused prepay less a 10% contract break fee (covers reservation costs). We can negotiate to 7.5% for multi-year strategic deals. Refund timeline: 60 days after final audit.
- True-ups / credits: unused prepaid capacity can be converted to platform credits that are usable across Redwood products (Dedicated compute credits applied to embeddings/hosted API at a 0.8x conversion rate) — this gives you flexibility. We allow one annual reallocation window per 12-month period.
- Invoice cadence: we can invoice annually on anniversary (preferred by us). For your fiscal mapping we can issue a pro forma invoice aligned to your Q-close (e.g., invoice dated 2026-12-31 for Yr1) while treating payment terms as agreed. We'll include a sample invoice mapping in the workbook.
- Accelerated scale-up: you can accelerate earlier tranche activation subject to availability; price on early activation: we can keep the contracted rate for the accelerated tranche if you notify 30 days in advance or apply a 5% acceleration fee for ad-hoc within 30 days.
- Monitoring & on-call: Ben confirms we provide customer-facing Prometheus metrics, per-route latency tracing, and a dedicated Slack channel + monthly architecture review. Dedicated on-call escalation for SLO breaches available as a paid add-on.

Ben: please paste the monitoring doc link and any technical caveats.
Marissa: please attach the two model sheets and one sample invoice.

Thanks,
Chloe
